newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent static in quiet trade, gas oil steady.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent static in quiet trade, gas oil steady.

text.p: IPE Brent futures were static in early trade with the market bereft of news to feed on and searching for direction.
August Brent was two cents lower at $17.75 a barrel by 1000 GMT while July gas oil was 25 cents down at $158.50 a tonne.

Dealers said the crude market looked very much rangebound as players weighed up the balance between fundamental weakness, based on fears of a supply glut, and some support coming from worries over ongoing delays to the Iraq/U.N. oil-for-food deal.
"The markets as a whole remain under fundamental pressure, and there should be further tests of the downside on this basis," said broker GNI in a daily report.

But worries persisted over a delay in resumed Iraqi crude exports after an Iraqi diplomat at the U.N. said on Wednesday Baghdad would not resume sales until money raised from the first six months of the agreement with the U.N. had all been spent.
This helped cancel out the bearish tone to the market, dealers said, with the market left idling as a result.
"Every time the market moves one way or the other it fails to break out of this range," one dealer said.
He and others cited support for Brent at $17.60 a barrel and resistance at $18.15 and then $18.30.
Gas oil, meanwhile, was hovering just below previous support at $160.00 a tonne but brokers thought it would regain that level and push just above it.
